title: Newton's Law of Gravitation
notes: **Law statement:** every particle in the universe attracts every other particle with a force proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them.
**Vector form:** $\vec{F}_{12} = -G\frac{m_1 m_2}{r^2}\hat{r}_{12}$. The negative sign indicates attraction; the force on 1 due to 2 points toward 2.
**Shell theorem:** a uniform spherical shell attracts an external particle as if all its mass were concentrated at its centre. Inside a uniform shell, the net gravitational force is zero.
**Why $G$ is so small:** gravitational force is much weaker than electromagnetic force. Between two protons, gravity is about $10^{-36}$ times weaker than the electric force.
confusion: Gravity is always attractive â€” there are no negative masses to repel. Unlike electric charge, which can be positive or negative.
The inverse-square law applies at all distances, but at very small distances other forces dominate.
Shell theorem only applies to uniform spherical shells or solid spheres.
practice: Calculate the gravitational force between two 1 kg masses separated by 1 m. Compare this with the weight of a 1 g mass on Earth.

universalFacts: Gravity is universal â€” it acts between any two masses anywhere in the universe.
The gravitational constant $G$ is the same everywhere in the universe.
Inside a uniform spherical shell, gravitational force is exactly zero at every point.
